introduction.text: In this lesson, you will learn about expressions used to talk about past events in Spanish. You will discover vocabulary related to time expressions and how to use them in sentences.
introduction.culturalNote: In many Spanish-speaking countries, storytelling is an important cultural tradition. Understanding past time expressions can help you appreciate these stories better.

exampleSentence.translation: Yesterday I went to the movies.

vocabulary.tip: Remember that 'ayer' always refers to the day before today.

exampleSentence.translation: The day before yesterday it rained a lot.

vocabulary.tip: Use 'anteayer' to talk about events that happened two days ago.

vocabulary.definition: The week before the current one.

exampleSentence.original: La semana pasada fui a la playa.
exampleSentence.translation: Last week I went to the beach.

vocabulary.tip: Use this phrase to refer to events that occurred in the previous week.

vocabulary.definition: The month before the current one.

exampleSentence.original: El mes pasado celebré mi cumpleaños.
exampleSentence.translation: Last month I celebrated my birthday.

vocabulary.tip: This can be used for events that happened in the previous month.

vocabulary.definition: Referring to an event that occurred two days in the past.

exampleSentence.original: Hice la tarea hace dos días.
exampleSentence.translation: I did the homework two days ago.

vocabulary.tip: Use 'hace' followed by a time expression to indicate how long ago something happened.
Use this structure to talk about specific years.

grammar.title: Using Past Time Expressions
grammar.explanation: Past time expressions help us specify when something happened. They can be used with different verb tenses, such as the preterite and imperfect. Remember to match the verb tense to the context of the sentence.

examples.translation: Yesterday I went to the park.
When I was a child, I played outside.

commonMistakes: Incorrect: Ayer estoy feliz. Correction: Ayer estuve feliz.
Incorrect: La semana pasada yo juego. Correction: La semana pasada jugué.

dialogue.title: Talking About Last Weekend
dialogue.context: A conversation between two friends discussing their past weekend.

lines.text: ¿Qué hiciste el fin de semana pasado?
lines.translation: What did you do last weekend?

lines.text: Fui a una fiesta el sábado.
lines.translation: I went to a party on Saturday.
How fun! And you, what did you do?

lines.text: El domingo, fui al cine con amigos.
lines.translation: On Sunday, I went to the movies with friends.
I love comedies. Did you like it?

culture.title: Celebrations in Spanish Culture
culture.text: In many Spanish-speaking countries, celebrations often include storytelling about past events. This can be a way to share family history or local legends, making past time expressions especially important.
culture.funFact: In Mexico, the Day of the Dead (Día de los Muertos) honors deceased loved ones through stories and memories.

keyPoints: Learned key past time expressions: ayer, anteayer, la semana pasada.
Understood how to use these expressions with different verbs.
Practiced dialogues to enhance conversational skills.
Gained cultural insights related to storytelling.
summary.nextSteps: Practice using these expressions in your own sentences and try to write about your last weekend!

exercises.explanation: 'La semana pasada' means 'last week' in English.
